newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on options-related sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on options-related sales.

text.p: Late selling which spread from the options pit and commercial selling near the close pressured CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.
A relatively light number in USDA's weekly export sales report also weighed on the market.
"The December (options) carried a high open interest. They were long calls and short puts and had to get them off and $2.70 was the strike price they targeted," a trader said.
The December options contracts expired Friday at 1201 CST.
But traders said corn was destined to decline.
"Corn never would have been higher if soybeans hadn't done what they did," a trader said. Soybeans closed strongly higher on active exports and a strong weekly soybean crush pace.
Corn export sales numbers were given a neutral to bearish nod, the traders said.

USDA early Friday released data showing the net exports of U.S. corn during the week ended November 7 at 797.3 million tonnes. That tally was below trade expectations for 900,000 to 1.1 million tonnes. The corn sales pace for 1996-97 was at 20.871 million tonnes, below 29.829 million a year ago.
Corn closed 1/2 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 1-3/4 at $2.69-1/2.
Key players included Goldenberg Hehmeyer with 3.5 million bushels purchased in the March and Tenco Inc buying three million December, traders said.
Smith Barney sold 2.5 million bushels of December and FIMAT Futures was on both sides of December for 1.5 million bushels, traders said.
Key moving averages for the December remained bearish but the contract moved above first reistance at $2.73 per bushel to post a session high of $2.75. Second resistance was at $2.76-1/2.
But the market faltered late and December reached a session low of $2.69 near the close, which was right on first support lines at $2.69-1/2 per bushel.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 57,000 contracts, below the 69,901 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, LIT America sold 300 December $2.70 puts at 1/4 to 1/2 cent, USA Trading sold 200 December $2.70 puts at 1/2 cent and Credit Agricole bought 500 December $2.70 puts at 1/4 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts, up from 20,716 traded Thursday.
